# Charging a card through Stripe

> A Kafka consumer that takes a payment request, charges the card through Stripe exactly once, records the result, and refunds the buyer if the product sold out in the meantime.

_Part of [domain/payments](../../units/domain/payments.md)_

Payment requests arrive on the `payments.requests` Kafka topic. `handlePayment` in [`PaymentController`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/api/payment.controller.ts#L15) hands each message to the shared Kafka consumer helper. That helper knows the response topic (`PAYMENTS_RESPONSES`) and the dead-letter topic (`PAYMENTS_DLQ`). The real work happens in `PaymentService.executePayment`. First, `executePayment` makes sure a `Payment` row exists for the request's idempotency key (a unique key that marks duplicate requests as the same request). It uses `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, then reads the row back. If the payment is already `COMPLETED`, `FAILED` or `REFUNDED`, it returns it at once. `PENDING` and `UNKNOWN` payments keep going. If a product is involved, a cheap stock check runs next. When stock is too low, it reports [`Domain_InsufficientStockError`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/api/payment.dto.ts#L91) and stops before touching Stripe. Then it calls Stripe's `createPaymentIntent` with the same idempotency key, with no DB transaction held open. If Stripe times out, the payment is marked `UNKNOWN`, because the card may have been charged. The error is rethrown so Kafka retries it. Afterwards, one "Finalize Transaction" DB transaction does the rest. On success it decrements stock with a version-checked `UPDATE`. It then sets the payment to `COMPLETED`, books the sale with [the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md), and writes the result to the outbox. On a Stripe failure it sets `FAILED` and writes a [`Domain_StripePaymentFailed`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/api/payment.dto.ts#L79) outbox message. If the stock update matches no rows, someone else bought the last item. In that case the service refunds the Stripe charge, marks the payment `REFUNDED`, and reports the stock error through the outbox. A later job, described in [Resolving payments stuck in UNKNOWN](resolving-unknown-payments.md), also settles `UNKNOWN` payments.

**Look at:** [payment.controller.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/api/payment.controller.ts) · [`PaymentService.executePayment` in payment.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/application/payment.service.ts#L65) · [`PostPaymentParamsDto` in payment.dto.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/api/payment.dto.ts#L35) · [`runInSpan` in tracing.utils.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/tracing.utils.ts#L11) · [`PaymentModule` in payment.module.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/payment.module.ts#L31)

## Pieces

- Payment request message shape: The validated payload on `payments.requests`: idempotency key, amount, buyer, order, Stripe payment method, and an optional product and quantity.
- [Idempotent creation of the payment row](idempotent-payment-insert.md): An insert with `ON CONFLICT ("idempotencyKey") DO NOTHING`, so a duplicate or retried message finds the existing payment rather than creating a second one.
- [Marking a timed-out Stripe charge as UNKNOWN](resolving-unknown-payments.md): If Stripe's outcome is unknown, the payment becomes `UNKNOWN` and the retry reuses the same Stripe idempotency key, so the original result comes back instead of a second charge.
- [Optimistic stock deduction](optimistic-stock-deduction.md): A cheap pre-check, then an `UPDATE "Product"` that only succeeds when `quantity >= :quantity` and bumps `version`. This is the real guard against overselling.
- [Refund when stock runs out after charging](refund-saga.md): When the stock update finds no row, the service refunds the Stripe payment intent outside the transaction, then marks the payment `REFUNDED` and notifies the caller.
- Publishing results through the outbox: Results and domain errors are written with `OutboxService.notify` inside the same DB transaction as the status change, so neither can be lost.
- Tracing spans around each step: [`runInSpan`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/tracing.utils.ts#L11) wraps each step (existing-payment check, Stripe call, finalize, refund) in an OpenTelemetry span.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| queue | `payments.requests` | Consumed by `handlePayment`; each message is one payment attempt. |
| queue | `PAYMENTS_RESPONSES (KafkaTopicGroup)` | Receives the success or failure result of each payment through the outbox. |
| queue | `PAYMENTS_DLQ (KafkaTopicGroup)` | Dead-letter topic for messages the consumer helper cannot process. Domain errors are not sent here. |
| database | `Payment` | Inserted as `PENDING` by idempotency key, then moved to `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `UNKNOWN` or `REFUNDED`; `providerRef` stores the Stripe id. |
| database | `Product` | Stock `quantity` is read for the pre-check and decremented with a `version` bump. |
| external | `Stripe` | `createPaymentIntent` charges the card, and `refundPaymentIntent` undoes the charge when stock is gone. Both use the idempotency key. |
| database | `Outbox (via OutboxService)` | Holds the result messages written in the same transaction as the payment update. |

## Also relies on

- [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md): Calls `LedgerService.recordMarketplaceSale` to book the sale into the clearing and platform-fee accounts after a successful charge.
- [Payment records and DTO service](payment-records.md): Uses the `Payment` model, its statuses and [`PaymentDtoService`](payment-records.md) to read and update payment rows.

## Watch out

- The stock check before Stripe is only a shortcut. The real guard is the version-checked `UPDATE` after the charge. That is why a customer can be charged and then refunded.
- A Stripe timeout does not mean failure. The payment becomes `UNKNOWN`, and the retry with the same key returns the original outcome.
- Domain errors (Stripe declined, insufficient stock) go out as normal outbox messages to the response topic. They do not go to the DLQ.
- The request field is `idempotency_key` (snake case), while the other fields are `camelCase`. A missing key throws [`Fatal_BadRequestError`](../common-errors/errors.md), because it is treated as an internal bug and not a user mistake.
